speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Since I delivered my Ministerial Statement on 26 March, 11 days ago, the pandemic has exploded.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In Singapore, we have progressively ratcheted up our measures, as the situation develops and the medical evidence comes in.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To minimise the risk of import of cases, we have severely restricted incoming flights and Singapore Airlines mounted dedicated flights to bring back Singaporeans who were overseas.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To limit local transmission, we have implemented comprehensive and complementary measures – safe-distancing, early identification and isolation of cases, and quarantine of close contacts.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These have kept the number of infections manageable, but in recent days, the numbers have been rising.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Local transmission has increased, and continues to grow.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These individuals mostly became infected when they were in close contact with infected persons at the social, workplace and family settings.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some clusters have emerged in our foreign worker dormitories.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To stay on top of the situation, the Government has taken a decisive step to pre-empt escalating infections.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is critical that every one of us keeps physical contact with others to a minimum.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Prime Minister addressed the nation last Friday.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Multi-Ministry Task Force announced an elevated set of safe distancing measures immediately after that.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These circuit breaker measures begin tomorrow and will last for four weeks.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The circuit breaker is essential, but we are acutely aware that it will be painful.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It will disrupt businesses and impact workers severely.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will miss face-to-face interactions with our friends and family.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many will be anxious about their jobs and families.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As the pandemic sweeps through the world, restrictions put in place in our trading partners will reduce demand for our exports even more.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must expect our overall GDP growth to take a further hit.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But we must take these hard decisions, make the difficult adjustments, and do all that we can in the next few months, to protect the lives of our people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Otherwise, if the outbreak escalates, the impact on lives and livelihood will be even worse.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must take short-term pains, to avoid even sharper pain later.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Let us all bear these immediate pains with fortitude and stay strong.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We obtained the President’s in-principle support for a draw of up to $17 billion from our past reserves towards this.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To further support our people and businesses during these extraordinary four weeks, when the circuit breaker measures are in place, I will bolster the Resilience Budget with a supplementary Solidarity Budget.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Unity, Resilience and Solidarity Budgets all build upon and reinforce each other.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Together, they represent our strong and decisive response to the economic and social consequences of the COVID-19 crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They have helped us to better understand the situation and quickly shape the support we now need.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The primary aim of this Solidarity Budget is to take further steps to save jobs and protect the livelihoods of our people during this temporary period of heightened measures.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also help businesses preserve their capacity and capabilities, to resume activities when the circuit breaker is lifted.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will also provide direct cash in hand for households, to help tide families through this difficult period.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: All of us will be affected by these necessary circuit breaker measures – some more than others.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To reach as many as we can, as fast as possible, the enhanced measures in the Solidarity Budget are broad-based.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, we will support our businesses to retain their workers and to stay viable.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In my Ministerial Statement on 26 March in this House, I mentioned the three Cs of support for firms’ immediate needs – cash, cost and credit.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will increase support in all three areas.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many firms cannot operate at all, or can only operate at a much reduced level in the coming weeks.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But they should still retain and pay their workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will enhance the Jobs Support Scheme to support them in doing so.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will help our workers keep their jobs and enable businesses to resume operations quickly when the circuit breaker is lifted.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I announced earlier in the Resilience Budget that the Jobs Support Scheme will subsidise 25% of the first $4,600 of gross monthly wages for all local employees.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I provided higher levels of wage subsidy for sectors that are more directly hit by the outbreak – 50% for firms in the food services sector and 75% for the aviation and tourism sectors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With the latest developments, almost every business and worker will be directly affected in the coming weeks.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will therefore enhance the Jobs Support Scheme for the month of April.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Rather, it means that this wage subsidy applies to every one of our over 1.9 million local employees.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But regardless of how much they earn, the maximum subsidy to the firms will be 75% of $4,600 per person, which is $3,450.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The salary limit of $4,600 is based on our median wage level of full-time employed residents.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The enhanced payout for April wages will be paid in this tranche.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Firms on GIRO and PayNow will start receiving the first Jobs Support Scheme payout next week.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Firms which are not on GIRO or PayNow will receive their payouts by cheque, starting about a week later.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The aim of this strong support is to directly reduce firms’ wage costs, to help them retain their workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I expect firms to make use of this Job Support Scheme to continue paying your workers and refrain from putting workers on no-pay leave during this period, or worse, retrenching them.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will monitor the situation carefully together with our tripartite partners and take action where needed.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many employers also hire foreign workers on work permits and S Passes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the same spirit, employers should take care of these workers who will also face difficulties during this circuit breaker period.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: By taking care of their workers, our firms can resume operations quickly once the heightened measures are lifted.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will reduce their cost, and relieve the pressures on their cash flow.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will help employers pay and take care of the upkeep of their workers, and prepare their workforce to restart when the circuit breaker is lifted.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Employers will receive the rebate as early as 21 April 2020.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government recognises that firms have been paying Foreign Worker Levies in normal times.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, in these exceptional times, we are temporarily redirecting resources back to the firms, to enable them to provide support for their foreign workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Minister for Manpower will share more details.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To further support businesses with costs, we are taking additional steps to make sure that our measures flow down to businesses.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I earlier announced a Property Tax Rebate of up to 100% for non-residential properties, for the tax payable in 2020.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This rebate is to help businesses deal with the impact of COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For most properties, the 100% Property Tax Rebate works out to slightly more than one month of rent.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Minister for Law will introduce a Bill tomorrow to let businesses and individuals defer certain contractual obligations, such as paying rent, repaying loans, or completing work, for a period.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This Bill will also ensure that property owners pass on the Property Tax Rebate in full, to tenants, as the Prime Minister mentioned in his address.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government will also continue to lead by example in supporting tenants.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will increase the rental waiver for industrial, office and agricultural tenants of Government agencies to one month, up from the 0.5 month’s rental waiver I announced at the Resilience Budget.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Stallholders in hawker centres managed by NEA or NEA-appointed operators will continue to enjoy three months of rental waivers, while commercial tenants will continue to receive two months of rental waivers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have touched on the first two Cs – cost and cash flow.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Last week, MAS, together with the financial institutions, also introduced a package of measures to help SMEs with temporary cashflow difficulties.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, SMEs can now opt to defer principal payments on their secured term loans till the end of the year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Banks and finance companies may also apply for low-cost funding through a new MAS Singapore Dollar facility, for new loans granted under the Enterprise Financing Scheme SME Working Capital Loan and Temporary Bridging Loan Programme.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: If they do so, they must commit to pass on the savings to their borrowers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The economy needs support and intervention in many different forms to go through this rough patch.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I urge all businesses, landlords, financial institutions and industry players to do your part, in channelling the Government’s support measures to firms, workers and households.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The enhancements I have just announced are to help workers who are employed by businesses to stay employed.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For self-employed persons, we have put in place the Self-Employed Person Income Relief Scheme, or SIRS, to provide direct cash assistance.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is the first time that we are providing direct cash support to self-employed persons on such a large scale.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They are a very diverse group, with different working hours and work arrangements.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some do this as full-time jobs, while others do this as part-time, to supplement their income.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some have been contributing CPF, while others have not.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Since the announcement on 26 March, the Minister for Manpower, NTUC Secretary-General and I, as well as our Government agencies, have received feedback from various self-employed persons whose livelihoods have been affected.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: During this circuit breaker period, more will see a further drop in income.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For instance, there are self-employed persons who are engaged in some employment work to supplement their incomes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Another group of self-employed persons bought an Executive Condominium some years ago.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Their income is now severely affected by the pandemic and they still have to support multiple family members' daily needs or medical bills.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: After considering the appeals, we will broaden the support for self-employed persons.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: On the other hand, many have shared their views that SIRS is overly generous.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some have asked – why do we allow self-employed persons with annual Net Trade Income of up to $100,000 to qualify.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As I explained earlier, self-employed persons are a very diverse group.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some are own account workers, like taxi drivers, who engage in a trade or business but do not employ any paid workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Others are sole proprietors, who own small businesses that have employees and a network of business relations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In these extraordinary times, many such self-employed persons are hard-hit.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I hope that by our helping them, they too can help others in their networks and their workers, and we keep the spirit of enterprise alive.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the spirit of tripartism, NTUC Secretary-General Ng Chee Meng has also agreed to step up and help administer the application and appeals for SIRS and support self-employed persons in need.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our approach now is to build up a network of support for as many as possible, as quickly as possible.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But done right, together, we can help many self-employed persons who are hard-hit.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: MOM will work closely with NTUC, to start processing appeals for SIRS as soon as possible.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have spoken about our support for firms and workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will also provide timely support for households to ensure that no household stands alone during this difficult period.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will bring forward $300 from the Care and Support – Cash payout that I announced earlier.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: On top of this, I will provide an additional $300, bringing the total to $600 for every adult Singaporean, aged 21 and above.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For the majority of Singaporeans who have provided their bank account details to the Government, the Solidarity Payment will be credited directly into their bank accounts by 14 April 2020.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The rest will receive the payment by cheque, to be issued in stages later, starting from 30 April 2020.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Other cash payouts under the Care and Support Package, which were earlier announced, will be brought forward to June 2020, instead of August 2020.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These include the remaining $300 or $600 from the higher tiers of the Care and Support – Cash payout; the additional $300 payout for each parent with at least one child aged 20 and below, and the $100 PAssion Card top-up, which will be given in cash, for Singaporeans aged 50 and above.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am very encouraged that many have written to me, my Ministerial colleagues and Members of Parliament, that they do not need the cash payouts and suggest that we give these to those who need the cash more.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I urge those who can, to donate to charities on the Giving.sg website or the Community Chest's Courage Fund, or to directly share it with others.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For those who still need more support, please approach our Social Service Offices and Community Centres to apply for new schemes such as the Temporary Relief Fund and the upcoming COVID-19 Support Grant, which is available from May 2020, as well as existing ComCare schemes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some Singaporeans will also be emotionally affected or distressed in this period.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, besides financial support, let us provide emotional and mental health support to our people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our community mental health support services will continue to provide care and support for clients through phone consultations, or home visits for those who may need more support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over the weekend, MSF announced that we will set up a 24/7 National Care Hotline.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The President had earlier given her in-principle support for the Government to draw up to $17 billion from past reserves to fund some of the measures in the Resilience Budget, to save jobs and businesses.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I also told Members then that I was prepared to propose to the President further draws on past reserves should it be necessary.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With the significantly stricter pre-emptive measures needed to protect Singaporeans and our families, it is now necessary for us to propose a further draw on past reserves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Specifically, this will be used to fund the enhanced Job Support Scheme, the Temporary Bridging Loan Programme and Enterprise Financing Scheme, and the Solidarity Payment to Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The remaining $1.1 billion will be funded from the fiscal space of this term of Government.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To effect the additional spending for the measures that I have announced today, I intend to seek Parliament's approval at the Committee of Supply to increase the supplementary estimates that were presented to Parliament on 26 March this year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will subsequently seek Parliament's approval to introduce a Revised Supplementary Supply Bill, on a Certificate of Urgency, that caters for the additional sums required.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is an unprecedented Budget, for extraordinary times.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government stands ready to provide further support, should it become necessary.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: (In Mandarin):   In order to stop the spread of the virus, we will adopt enhanced safe distancing measures for one month.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Apart from those providing essential services and industries in the key economic sectors, all other workplaces will be closed starting from tomorrow.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With rising local transmission cases, if we do not further enhance our precautionary measures, the situation will quickly worsen, causing our healthcare system to be overwhelmed.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our immediate task is to protect the safety of our people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: However, if we lose our health or even our lives, what remains will only be regrets.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As such, to protect the safety and health of Singaporeans, everyone must strictly observe these precautionary measures.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These measures will seriously impact the operations of our enterprises and people’s daily lives.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is the third Budget announced by the Government within a short span of two months.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The main purpose is to keep enterprises afloat, help them retain their workers’, so that everyone can tide over this extraordinary period and persevere.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also legislate that the property owners must pass on the property tax rebate in full to their tenants.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will increase the rental waiver for industrial, office and agricultural tenants of Government agencies, from half month to one month.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In addition, we will take further steps to help businesses obtain credit through the Enterprise Financing Scheme and Temporary Bridging Loan Programme so that they can continue to operate.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also broaden the eligibility criteria for the Self-Employed Person Income Relief Scheme to include self-employed persons who earn some salary from part-time employment and those who reside in property with Annual Value not more than $21,000.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: During this period, many businesses who employ foreign workers are not able to operate.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To help these businesses cope with labour cost and make sure that they continue to look after their foreign workers, we will waive the Foreign Worker Levy for the month of April, and provide additional Foreign Worker Levy Rebate.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For each work permit or S pass holder, the employer will receive a rebate of $750.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At the same time, in order to lighten the burden for families, all adult Singaporeans will receive a one-off Solidarity Payment of $600.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I announced earlier that Singaporeans would receive a cash payout under the Care and Support Package.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Now, under the Solidarity Payment, I will first disburse $300 from the Care and Support Package and add an additional $300.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In other words, every adult Singaporean will receive a Solidarity payment of $600 in cash early.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I mentioned before that, if necessary, we would draw more from the past reserves to fund new measures.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have received in-principle support from President Halimah to draw on past reserves to fund the new measures announced today.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To many businesses, this coming month will be very difficult.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I hope that these new measures will help them tide over this difficult period.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In these extraordinary times, we must continue to care for one another, particularly the elderly and the vulnerable.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must pay attention to our health, personal hygiene and cultivate good habits.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So long as we stay united, stay healthy, while continuing to protect jobs, enterprises and secure our future, Singapore will eventually come out of the difficult situation, overcome the pandemic and emerge stronger.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: (In English): Mr Speaker, Sir, I will now conclude in English.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is a generational crisis with no precedent.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have brought all our resources and administrative capacity to bear, to mount a national effort for our workers, businesses and families, to protect both lives and livelihoods.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have the plans and the financial resources to carry out these plans without burdening future generations with the bill.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are grateful to our founding generation for their foresight and discipline.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The key now is how we can pull together, in solidarity, as a nation, to implement these plans and make adjustments as the situation continues to evolve.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: COVID-19 is testing nations worldwide and revealing more about government, about each society, our identity and the values that hold us together.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Though the pandemic is global, the impact on each country depends greatly on the different actions and responses of each government and their people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Trust and confidence of our people in the government are critical.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our people must understand what we are facing and support what we are doing.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is why we have been forthcoming and transparent with Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As Minister Lawrence Wong said, every person is, in fact, on the frontline.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Every Singaporean can make a difference in slowing down the spread of the virus today.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To keep out the virus, every one of us must play our part.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Be socially responsible by staying home, staying safe and staying healthy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As we do so, we must keep our spirits up and look out for each other, especially our seniors and the more vulnerable.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our Government agencies as well as many volunteers are contributing their best to care for our vulnerable groups.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Let us unite, demonstrate our resilience, stay united and press on in solidarity.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I suggest that should there be clarifications, I will fold them into the debate subsequently.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Clerk will now proceed to read the order of the day.
